title: Word Squares
summary: Given an array of distinct strings, generate all possible word squares using these strings.
statement: Given an array of distinct strings, generate all possible word squares using these strings. Words can be reused. Return the word squares in any order. A word square is valid if the kth row and column match the same string for all k.
constraints: 1 <= words.length <= 1,000; all words are unique lowercase English strings of the same length n, 1 <= n <= 4.
Build every n-row square whose kth row equals its kth column. A dictionary word may be used more than once.
Outer answer order is arbitrary; row order inside each square matters. Do not emit duplicate squares.
hints: After choosing some rows, the next row already has a required prefix.
Index dictionary words by prefix, then recursively try only words matching the next column prefix.
At depth d, required = previous_rows[0][d] + ... + previous_rows[d-1][d]. Try each match, recurse, and undo.
The prefix constraint checks each new mirrored pair. Copy completed row lists; do not mark dictionary words as globally used.
editorial: The rows already chosen determine the first d characters of row d. A prefix index avoids scanning unrelated words at each branch. Every matching choice preserves symmetry among chosen rows, so a depth-n path is a complete square. Unique dictionary words give one path per square, but the same word can legitimately occupy multiple rows. With W words, prefix strings cost O(W*n^2) storage; search is output-sensitive with the stated loose worst-case bound.

tests.explanation: Both ball | area | lead | lady and wall | area | lead | lady have matching rows and columns.
The two squares begin baba | abat | baba and end atal or atan. Reusing baba is allowed and necessary.
